rv.q: It’s a stunning achievement, which takes the popular but very different elements of retro pop music, agitprop and soap opera, melts them in the crucible of 50 years of social trauma and forges something potent, gorgeous and unlike any big-ticket musical I’ve seen before.
This stylish production set on the iconic Park Hill estate is a terrific blend of power and heart.
A deeply moving, monumental musical that really matters … deserves to be a huge hit.
It's jubilant and defiant, with the emotional force of a juggernaut.
Chris Bush’s Standing at the Sky’s Edge announces itself and the mixture of sweet and tart, tender and tough, that will drive this exhilarating, big-hearted musical.

This remains a huge achievement by Hastie and Bush, one of our most prolific and arresting writers: a bold step forward for musical theatre, that brings northern, working-class steel to the South Bank.
It's a stirring tribute to the resili[ence]...
Yet this often lovely piece of theatre also falls short of its own ambition.

Provoking fevered reactions – many audible gasps or sobs were heard after a variety of plot beats – while being resolutely, brazenly assured in its craft, makes Standing at the Sky’s Edge a towering feat of contemporary musical theatre.
The surging storylines finally coalesce to blow us away in a crescendo of love, heartbreak and the acceptance that life goes on.

A joyful, gritty show with fire in its heart … A musical set on a Sheffield housing estate may not be the easiest pitch to Broadway producers - but they'd be missing out on the best British musical in decades. … Singer/songwriter Richard Hawley and playwright Chris Bush have fashioned a work that is both site-specific and universally epic.

cn.t: Critics hail this Sheffield-set musical as a stunning achievement and the best new British musical in years, praising its emotional power, Richard Hawley's stirring score, and its ambitious triple narrative spanning six decades of social change.
